key_insight: SCAPS-1D optimization suggests that an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 stack can strongly improve charge extraction and push CNGS thin-film solar-cell efficiency to 28.44%.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical design rules for absorber thickness, doping, defects, interfaces, and resistive losses to guide experimental development of high-efficiency, earth-abundant thin-film photovoltaics.
method: Modeled a CNGS solar cell with In2S3 electron-transport and MoTe2 hole-transport layers in SCAPS-1D.
Analyzed band alignment, electric field, carrier profiles, and generation-recombination behavior.
Swept key parameters including thickness, doping, defect densities, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination intensity.
evidence_signal: The optimized simulated device reached 28.44% PCE with VOC = 0.984 V, JSC = 34.39 mA/cm2, and FF = 84.04% under AM1.5G at 300 K.
watch_item: The result is computational and depends on idealized material/interface parameters, so experimental fabrication, stability, and defect control may reduce realized performance.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
